thread.title: UPDATE: McDonald's, Walmart and other U.S. stocks that could rise from the ashes of a correction

author: morningstar.com
title: UPDATE: McDonald's, Walmart and other U.S. stocks that could rise from the ashes of a correction
text:
By Barbara Kollmeyer, MarketWatch
Critical information for the U.S. trading day
A rocky October looks likely to treat investors with volatility up to the bitter end.
As Monday's session showed, there may be plenty of up and down action left to toss this market around (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/mondays-fading-stock-market-rally-is-evidence-that-the-worst-is-far-from-over-for-wall-street-2018-10-29). Investors who haven't already done so may now start battening down the hatches (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/if-you-werent-yet-worried-about-the-stock-market-you-should-be-now-2018-10-30). Don't look to November and midterms for any relief, says CrackedMarket's (https://cracked.market/) Jani Ziedins.
"No matter what happens election day, we should expect a knee-jerk of selling as investors from the losing party dump stocks before the other side can wreck the country," he says.
If you're struggling to rationalize this market, then stop and check out our call of the day from traders Howard Lindzon and Ivaylo Ivanhoff, who lay out how to navigate a market correction via their Momentum Monday video (http://howardlindzon.com/) . Among other things, they highlight a handful of stocks -- household names in some cases -- poised to lead when the dust has settled.
A big name on their list is Walmart (WMT), already standing out as a leader and holding up the market as institutional investors have swapped it out for Amazon (AMZN) . The online retailer is down 23% in October versus a 6% gain for its mostly bricks and mortar rival that has a "massive digital appetite," notes Lindzon.
Starbucks (SBUX) and its "addicted base" is another one to watch coming out of the correction, says Lindzon, the co-founder of StockTwits. He's even more excited about McDonald's (MCD), praising the fast-food giant's hustle to improve its food, coffee and stores. Set for a 3.6% gain in October, McDonald's is a "great company that's viable on big dips," and is more of a technology company than it ever was, says Lindzon.
Other possible leaders mentioned: Cadence Design Systems (CDNS) , Audiocodes (AUDC) , CME Group (CME) , PayPal (PYPL) and even Goldman Sachs (GS).
"In a bull market, [Goldman] could start being valued more as a tech holding company. It could be a long-term play," says Lindzon.
While you're at it, it's worth checking out Steve Sjuggerud's Daily Wealth blog (https://dailywealth.com/), where he talks about how the surprising big champions from the last great "melt-up" of 1998 to early 2000 -- biotechs -- are getting ready for a repeat performance.
The market
Dow , S&P 500 and Nasdaq futures are struggling to hold onto some green after a bigger bump in Asia. Monday's volatile session (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/stocks-set-to-attempt-rebound-after-last-weeks-slide-2018-10-29) saw the Dow swung more the 900 points, but finishing lower, along with the S&P and Nasdaq .
Gold is off some, the dollar is up a little, notably against the and crude is mixed.
Check out the Market Snapshot column for the latest action.
Europe also struggled, while Asia finished mixed (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/asian-markets-mixed-as-us-china-trade-tensions-rear-up-again-2018-10-29), but with a 1% gain for the Shanghai Composite .
The stat
The Nasdaq saw its 8th session of a 1% or greater loss, the most since August 2011 when it also logged a string of eight straight losses. If the Nasdaq logs one more 1% down day, it'll be the most in a calendar month since Nov. 2008, when it also had nine, according to Dow Jones Market Data.
The chart
How volatile has October been? Our chart of the day, from The Daily Shot (https://blogs.wsj.com/dailyshot/2018/10/30/the-daily-shot-are-good-times-over-for-defense-contractors/), shows how the S&P 500 hasn't seen such rocky times since the so-called "volmageddon" of February:
The Quote:
'I think that we will make a great deal with China and it has to be great, because they've drained our country.' -- That was POTUS in an interview with Fox News late Monday (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/trump-says-he-will-make-a-great-deal-with-china-on-trade-but-has-more-tariffs-at-the-ready-2018-10-30), with a comment that gave a boost to Asian stocks and U.S. stock futures at least for awhile. It comes a day after reports the White House is getting lob billions more in import duties at China if a deal can't be reached.
Meanwhile, Fox News' Shepard Smith rejected any White House scaremongering over migrant caravans (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/fox-news-shepard-smith-debunks-trumps-migrant-caravan-rhetoric-there-is-no-invasion-2018-10-29). (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/fox-news-shepard-smith-debunks-trumps-migrant-caravan-rhetoric-there-is-no-invasion-2018-10-29) Elsewhere, come reports Trump may target (https://www.cnbc.com/2018/10/30/trump-plans-to-terminate-birthright-citizenship.html) the rights of babies born in the U.S. to non-citizens and unauthorized immigrants.
The buzz
Rolling out results this morning, General Electric (GE) is up despite a miss (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/ges-stock-edges-up-after-profit-and-sales-miss-plan-to-reorganize-power-business-2018-10-30), after saying it will break up its power unit. Coca-Cola (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/coca-colas-stock-gains-after-earnings-and-revenue-rise-above-expectations-2018-10-30)(KO) is up on beats, while Pfizer, (PFE) is down after a revenue miss (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/pfizers-stock-falls-after-profit-beats-but-revenue-misses-2018-10-30). Mastercard (MA) , Under Armour (UAA) and Allergan (AGN) are also on the list. In London, BP (BP.LN) earnings soared (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/bp-earnings-soar-on-stronger-oil-prices-2018-10-30-44855336) on strong oil prices.
After the close, we'll get Facebook (FB) , EBay (EBAY) , Amgen (AMGN) , FireEye (FEYE) and Electronic Arts (EA) .

Data showed the Case-Shiller home price index hitting a 20-month low (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/house-price-gains-lurch-to-a-20-month-low-case-shiller-says-2018-10-30). Consumer confidence and home ownership stats are also on the docket for Tuesday.
